thread:
tess: quick FYI — noticed a short burst of 502s hitting /v1/generate from a small set of client IPs, about ~120 errors over 8m. Any quick places to grab traces + a lightweight triage checklist?

nate: pinging infra. first things: dashboard + example request-id. dash: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/5G7-errors/4xx-5xx-overview?var-route=/v1/generate

infra-bot: alert: route:/v1/generate 502-rate spike 120 events in 8m (severity: P3) — triggered at 1755550005

maya: easiest query to get top client IPs in logs: 
```
index=prod-logs route="/v1/generate" status=502 | top client_ip by count limit=10
```

maya: to pull sample traces once you have a request-id: 
```
curl -s "https://traces.redwood.internal/api/traces?request_id=<REQUEST_ID>" | jq . | less
```

liam: quick checklist I use: 1) grab 3 sample request-ids (early/mid/end of spike) 2) check ingress LB logs for 502 vs upstream 3) lookup model-variant fallback logs 4) check kvcache timeout metric (kvcache.timeout.count) for same window

liam: runbook (short): https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/502-triage-cheatsheet — suggests checking prefix-cache timeouts + backend connection resets first.

nate: if it's client IP specific, also check rate-limit buckets and any WAF rules: https://console.redwood.internal/observability/waf-activity?ip=<IP>

maya: low-effort alert tuning suggestion: if this is frequent noisy bursts from single IPs, consider debouncing to 3m and using cardinality-based suppression: 
- change alert: `alert when rate(502) > 0.02 for 3m unless top-n clients > 5`

liam: +1. For now don't lower sensitivity, prefer debounce and add a note to the alert description explaining false-positive sources (e.g., retries from bad clients).

tess: this is great — I'll collect 3 request-ids and paste them here, then grab traces. Also will try the kvcache metric and WAF link. Thanks! :thumbsup:

nate: if you post one request-id I'll fetch the trace and post the link.

oncall-bot: runbook excerpt: "When 5xx spike on ingress: 1) capture request-id 2) check LB and upstream status codes 3) verify model fallback logs 4) escalate to eng-runtime if upstream timeouts or kvcache errors persist"

tess: posted two ids: req_20260317_01 and req_20260317_02 — grabbing the third and will drop traces here in ~5m.

nate: grabbing req_20260317_01 -> https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/aaaa1111 (shared)

maya: grabbing req_20260317_02 -> https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/bbbb2222 (shared)

liam: early look — both traces show a short upstream connection reset at the model host, and kvcache.timeout.count has small spike aligned at +1m. Could be transient overload on that shard.

tess: ok will open a small follow-up with eng-runtime if we see more. Thanks everyone, will update thread after follow-up.
